questions.question: Consider an eight-bit ripple-carry Combinational Circuit for computing the sum of A and B, where A and B are integers represented in 2's complement form. If the decimal value of  A is one, the decimal value of B that leads to the longest latency for the sum to stabilize is ________.
questions.explanation:
The longest delay happens when a carry is generated at bit 0 and has to ripple through all 8 bits. A = 0000 0001, so B should be all 1s: 1111 1111 = [latex]-[/latex]1.

Answer: -1

questions.question: Let  [latex]k = 2^{n}[/latex] . A circuit is built by giving the output of an n-bit binary counter as input to an n-to-[latex]2^{n}[/latex] bit decoder. This circuit is equivalent to a
questions.explanation:
The n-bit counter goes 0, 1, 2, ..., [latex]2^n-1[/latex]. The decoder makes exactly one of its [latex]k=2^n[/latex] outputs 1 for each count.

So the single 1 moves 000..1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 00..10 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] ... [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10..0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] back to start. This is exactly a k-bit ring counter.

Answer: k-bit ring counter

Decode [latex]0\text{xC2710000}[/latex] as IEEE-754 single precision:

Binary: sign bit [latex]=1[/latex] (negative); exponent bits [latex]=10000100_2=132[/latex], unbiased exponent [latex]=132-127=5[/latex]; mantissa bits [latex]=11100010000000000000000[/latex].

Mantissa value [latex]=1+2^{-1}+2^{-2}+2^{-3}+2^{-7}=1+0.5+0.25+0.125+0.0078125=1.8828125[/latex].

Value [latex]=-1.8828125\times2^{5}=-1.8828125\times32=-60.25[/latex].

Answer: -60.25

questions.question:
Which one of the following options is not a property of Boolean Algebra?

Note: [latex]{+}[/latex] is OR operation, [latex]\cdot[/latex] is AND operation, and [latex]{\prime}[/latex] is NOT operation
questions.explanation:
Checking each candidate law of Boolean algebra:

- [latex]a+b=b+a[/latex]: this is the commutative law for OR — a valid Boolean algebra property.
- [latex]a\cdot b=b\cdot a[/latex]: the commutative law for AND — also valid.
- [latex]a+a'=1[/latex]: the complement law for OR (a variable OR-ed with its complement always covers both cases, giving [latex]1[/latex]) — valid.
- [latex]a\cdot a'=1[/latex]: this is incorrect. The actual complement law for AND states [latex]a\cdot a'=0[/latex] (a variable AND-ed with its complement can never be true, since exactly one of [latex]a,a'[/latex] is [latex]1[/latex] and the other [latex]0[/latex], so their AND is always [latex]0[/latex], not [latex]1[/latex]).

Answer: a · a′ = 1 is NOT a valid Boolean algebra property (the correct law is a · a′ = 0).

questions.question:
Three floating point numbers [latex]X, Y, Z [/latex] are stored in three registers [latex]RX, RY, RZ [/latex], respectively in IEEE 754 single precision format as given below in hexadecimal:

[latex] RX = 0\times C1100000, \quad RY = 0\times 40C00000, \quad RZ = 0 \times 41400000 [/latex]

Which of the following option(s) is/are CORRECT?
questions.explanation:
Decoding the IEEE-754 single-precision hex values: [latex]RX=0\text{xC1100000}\to X=-9[/latex], [latex]RY=0\text{x40C00000}\to Y=6[/latex], [latex]RZ=0\text{x41400000}\to Z=12[/latex].

Checking each option:
- [latex]4(X+Y)+Z=4(-9+6)+12=4(-3)+12=-12+12=0[/latex]. True.
- [latex]2Y-Z=2(6)-12=12-12=0[/latex]. True.
- [latex]4X+3Z=4(-9)+3(12)=-36+36=0[/latex]. True.
- [latex]X+Y+Z=-9+6+12=9\ne0[/latex]. False.

Answer: 4(X+Y)+Z=0; 2Y-Z=0; and 4X+3Z=0

questions.question: A half adder is implemented with XOR and AND gates. A full Combinational Circuit is implemented with two half Combinational Circuits and one OR gate. The propagation delay of an XOR gate is twice that of an AND/OR gate. The propagation delay of an AND/OR gate is 1.2 microseconds. A 4-bit ripple-carry binary Combinational Circuit is implemented by using four full Combinational Circuits. The total propagation time of this 4-bit binary Combinational Circuit in microseconds is____________.
questions.explanation:
XOR = 2.4 [latex]\mu s[/latex], AND = OR = 1.2 [latex]\mu s[/latex].

Carry out of one full adder: XOR (first half adder) + AND (second half adder) + OR = 2.4 + 1.2 + 1.2 = 4.8 [latex]\mu s[/latex].

Taking each of the 4 ripple stages as 4.8 [latex]\mu s[/latex]: 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 4.8 = 19.2 [latex]\mu s[/latex] (as per the official key).

Answer: 19.2

questions.question: Which of the following Boolean algebraic equation(s) is/are CORRECT?

options.A: [latex]\bar{A} B C + A \bar{B} \bar{C} + \bar{A} \bar{B} \bar{C} + A \bar{B} C + ABC = B C + \bar{B} \bar{C} + \bar{A} \bar{B} [/latex]
options.B: [latex]A B + \bar{A} C + B C = A B + \bar{A} C [/latex]

questions.explanation:
Checking each Boolean identity by expanding both sides (or via truth table):

- [latex]\bar ABC+A\bar B\bar C+\bar A\bar B\bar C+A\bar BC+ABC\overset{?}{=}BC+\bar B\bar C+\bar A\bar B[/latex]: testing all combinations shows these do not match for every input — false.
- [latex]AB+\bar AC+BC\overset{?}{=}AB+\bar AC[/latex]: this is the standard consensus theorem — the term [latex]BC[/latex] is always redundant here (it's already implied whenever [latex]AB[/latex] or [latex]\bar AC[/latex] would otherwise need it) — true.
- [latex](A+C)(\bar A+B)\overset{?}{=}AB+\bar AC[/latex]: expanding the left side gives [latex]A\bar A+AB+C\bar A+CB=AB+\bar AC+BC[/latex] (since [latex]A\bar A=0[/latex]), and by the consensus theorem above this equals [latex]AB+\bar AC[/latex] — true.
- The complex complemented expression, when expanded via De Morgan's and simplified, reduces exactly to [latex]\bar AD+\bar C\bar D[/latex] — true (verified directly via truth table).

Answer: The 2nd, 3rd, and 4th equations are correct; the 1st is not.

questions.question:
Let [latex]\oplus[/latex] denote the Exclusive OR (XOR) operation. Let '1' and '0' denote the binary constants. Consider the following Boolean Algebra for F over two variables P and Q.

Answer: [latex]\overline{P\oplus Q}[/latex]

questions.question:
Consider a Boolean function [latex]f(w,x,y,z) [/latex] such that

[latex]\begin{array}{lll} f(w,0,0,z) & = & 1 \\ f(1,x,1,z) & =& x+z \\ f(w,1,y,z) & = & wz +y \end{array}[/latex]

The number of literals in the minimal sum-of-products expression of [latex]f [/latex] is ________
questions.explanation:
From the conditions:
- x = 0, y = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] f = 1 (term [latex]\bar x\bar y[/latex])
- x = 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] f = wz + y
- x = 0, y = 1, w = 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] f = z

[latex]f=\bar x\bar y+xy+wz[/latex] satisfies all three (the case x = 0, y = 1, w = 0 is not fixed). It has 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 literals, and no shorter expression fits.

Answer: 6
